BiblicalUsage: To give in Ezra and Daniel is the movement of kings and of God. The enemies warn that a rebuilt Jerusalem will not pay toll or tribute, the king's treasury gives whatever the house of God needs, Daniel asks the king to give him time, and the Most High gives the kingdom to whomsoever He will.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every gift in these books flows one way or the other from God's hand: kings give from their treasuries, but God gives the kingdoms themselves. Ezra's king gives from the treasury, and Daniel's God gives kingdoms — the smaller gift serves the greater.
